data.text:
$GRAB| Does it have MOAT?🧵

TLDR: Can a business with NO MOAT get 0% to 70-75% Market Share and soon to be 90-95%? 

Grab Holdings operates as Southeast Asia's leading AI SuperApp, integrating ride-hailing (Mobility), food/grocery delivery (Deliveries), digital payments, lending,other financial services and B2B solutions across eight countries: Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, Cambodia, and Myanmar. Critics, particularly bearish investors, frequently argue that Grab lacks a sustainable economic moat that shields it from competitors and ensures long term profitability. They point to the commoditized nature of ride-hailing and delivery services, where low switching costs for users and drivers could erode market position.

Yet, this perspective fails to account for Grab's remarkable ascent from a nascent startup to a dominant force holding approximately 70-75% market share(from 0%) in core mobility segments across eight countries. Moreover, the company's achievement of GAAP operating leverage in the third quarter of 2025, marked by positive operating profit and robust revenue growth, underscores a maturing business model that defies the "no moat" narrative. 

Grab's journey to market dominance began with a keen insight into Southeast Asia's unique challenges. Founded in 2012 by Anthony Tan as MyTeksi, the company addressed fundamental issues like safety, accountability, and regulatory compliance in fragmented urban transport markets.Unlike global giants such as Uber, which entered the region with a one size fits-all approach, Grab localized its offerings incorporating motorbike rides for traffic congested cities, cash payments for underbanked populations, and hyperlocal features tailored to cultural nuances. $GRAB won and acquired $UBER in 2018, consolidating its leadership, in certain market $GRAB has nearly 95-98% market share. 

Now, what is $GRAB Actual MOAT? Why short sellers were so successful in pushing more than 1 billion shares from "Dumb money" to "Smart money?. That hasn't changed since Sept/Oct 2025 high, where "Dumb Money" was the main seller along with short sellers selling pressure. 

I have to credit @alexhungate to strengthen $GRAB  MOAT since he joined the company in early 2022 and launched GrabUnlimited along with other strategic initiatives that got us to Positive GAAP Operating Leverage today. 

If you read my prior posts, you would see me citing the similarity of $GRAB Business model to $AMZN or $COST. $GRAB has low-margin core business (Mobility/Delivery) at early phase like $AMZN E-commerce, where it was historical loss-making but dominating most of revenue growth to build a massive ecosystem to acquire 300m+ Prime membership. Or $COST members that save thousands shopping at CostCo knowing they will get a better price than anywhere else, and of course the legend $1.50 hotdog and $4.99 rotisserie chicken. Btw, most of Food delivery done on $GRAB are done by small motobike/Scooter where fuel cost is very low, especially at current gasoline price. 

During Covid Time toward 2022, @AnthonyPY_Tan and @alexhungate understood the nonstop Price War was unsustainable, they decided to focus on providing more value to customers to differentiate the SuperApp from others, AKA moving to customer-obsessed from competitor-obsessed. 

Here is $GRAB Strucural MOAT:

~Ecosystem and Flywheel
~HyperLocal & Regulatory Navigation
~Data and Operational efficiency at Scale
~Ecosystem expansion

GRAB SuperApp creates  powerful cross-service synergies. A ride user can use  food delivery, then payments/lending, book travel, dine-out or start a small restaurant. GrabUnulimited gets the highest discount in all services sold on the platform at $4.99 a month. GRAB has the largest drviers' network in SEA, and is behind on drivers, meaning revenue could be 50% higher if they have more drivers, hence GRAB is seeking autonomous, drone and robotic for its core business. Goal for this region is 300m+ GrabUnlimited members or $15-$25B a month in just subscription. And $5-$10 a month is abt less than 1% of average monthly household income in SEA! 

By the third quarter of 2025, Grab reported 48 million monthly transacting users, a 6 million increase year-over-year, with daily transactions surging 27% and gross merchandise value (GMV) per user rising 7%. This ecosystem extends beyond commoditized services into higher-margin areas like fintech and advertising. Grab's financial services arm, including GrabPay and lending, is scaling toward a $1 billion loan book, leveraging transaction data for AI-driven credit scoring and fraud detection. 

Advertising revenue is another growth engine, with active advertisers up 15% YoY and average spend per advertiser jumping 41%, driven by targeted, data-rich campaigns.Competitors like Gojek (strong in Indonesia) or Foodpanda struggle to replicate this breadth, as Grab's integrated model raises switching costs and creates a "walled garden" effect, much like China's WeChat or Meituan.

Creative service like Dine-Out is very recent, and has 70-80% margin by charging a commission where Restaurants/small businesses want to buy visibility. This is one of the best new feature launched that attracted 1/3 of new recent new users. 

Part of $GRAB MOAT is flexibility of Payment, and the willingness to tailor services/businesses to local needs/cultural structure where regulation can be very complex. Data and operational scale further fortify Grab's defenses. Processing over 2 billion daily events, Grab's proprietary Hyperlocal AI engine optimizes routing, pricing, and personalization, reducing delivery times by 15% YoY while improving margins. Regulatory moats add another layer; Grab holds licenses for payments and finance across multiple countries, enabling it to serve underbanked segments that global players might overlook. In deliveries, Grab is building merchant lock-in through initiatives like GrabSignatures exclusive restaurant partnerships that offer lower commissions in exchange for platform exclusivity.

Q3 2025 financial results illustrate Grab's operating leverage, where revenue growth outpaces costs, signaling a shift from growth at all costs to sustainable profitable growth. Revenue climbed 22% YoY to $873 million, fueled by 24% GMV growth in on-demand services. Adjusted EBITDA soared 51% to $136 million, reflecting a 19% margin, while the company posted a $17 million net profit and $27 million in operating profit. FCF improved dramatically, reaching $283 million on a trailing 12-month basis, up $185 million YoY. With $7.4 billion in gross cash liquidity, up from $6.1 billion the prior year, Grab is well-positioned for investments like deploying more autonomous, robotic and drone investment/acquisition(Infermove). These figures counter bearish claims by demonstrating that Grab's scale is translating into GAAP-level efficiencies, with partner incentives (4.8% of mobility GMV and 4.4% of deliveries) poised for reduction as automation advances.

In addition, Bears often cited $GRAB does not know how to use its huge cash balance, however, the recent Superbank IPO more than 4x GRAB initial investment. Along with all other investment in the last 2-3 years, GRAB is up 400-500% to current estimate of $4.4B in equity. Meaning $7.4B Cash + $4.4B Equity= $11.8B. This kind of return outperformed almost all Funds in the US and anywhere. And Of course, "Dumb money" that sold believed the Bears and sold more than 1B shares in just 4 quarters and continuning, where Instituional onwership climbed from 57% to ~84%. One of the fastest wealth exchange I seen from my years in the stock market. 

Grab's moat is not illusory but a robust construct of network effects, data-driven innovation, regulatory savvy, and ecosystem synergies that explain its 70-75% market share and Q3 2025 operating leverage. While bears focus on commoditization, they overlook how Grab's super-app model and execution under solid leadership create durable barriers in one of the world's fastest-growing digital regions. 

The SuperApp flywheel further dismantles the commoditization argument. Cross-service usage ride users trying deliveries, then payments/lending lowers acquisition costs, boosts retention, and creates stickiness that pure play competitors can't replicate.

In essence, the bears are wrong because they evaluate Grab through a Western lens treating it as "just another Uber" in commoditized markets while ignoring the realities of Southeast Asia's digital economy: a founder-led, culturally native super-app that has built structural, compounding advantages. $UBER is actually learning on $GRAB and trying to mirror the SuperApp of NA. 

And Lastly, this is only 6.5% Penetration to 700m SEA population and 14% thesis of "Bottom of Pyramid" Core up to 5 billion people to service. GRAB SuperApp growth is far from maturity, and the thesis is just getting started!

If you enjoy this kind of thread, slap the like/repost/bookmark to please the X Algo.      

If you want to read/support my in-depth analyses, consider subscribe.

Alright, that is it. 

Not Financial Advice!

192.7m shares shorted gotta cover at some point.

Meaning, most of 192.7m shares shorted are extremely red. 

So far, Bears were only good at scaring "dumb money", Institutional ownership rocketed from 
55% Q3 2024
=> ~84% Q3 2025

In 4 quarters, "Smart money" took 27-28% ownership from "Dumb money". 

In this thread, I want to discuss more about how much it costed short sellers so far in Margin interest and potentially losses. 

Roughly $800m was borrowed or 192.7m shares(estimate) and around $50m on Margin Interest.

On paper, if they all covered today, they would be down around $200m+ $50m= $250m for institutions and funds that are shorting $GRAB. 

But "Dumb money" will suffer the highest loss due to this 27-28% exit or around 1 Billion share. 

If you followed my posts consistently, you would see most asking about daily price action instead of Fundamental. Or how they were nervous of price action, not Operating Leverage, not all the new verticlal growth recently. 

From Q3 2024 - Q3 2025
~GRAB grew revenue average at 24.2%. 
~Achieved GAAP Operating Leverage 
~Indo Govt is forcing $GOTO to sell Delivery/Mobility segment to $GRAB for $1.5B(leaked Info). COO Alex Hungate and CFO Peter said they won't buy if the price is not right. 
~Market share is inching above 70% in SEA, and with this $GOTO, it will go 90-95% market share. Bears often cited $GRAB has 0 moat, then explain to me why 0% to 90-95% market share?

So you must ask, did major institutions coordinated this drama to "swallow the float" as I put it since Feb 2025? Absolutely, and "Dumb money" bought the manipulation!

You don't sell a company that is 
~Accelerating growth 
~Achieve Monopoly
~$7.4B Cash with Little Debt 

Reason that "Dumb money" sold?
"Oh share price was going down"
"Oh I didnt need to understand the business, I only care about price action right now" 
"Oh I must have 100% gain Every 30-days"

These legend investors/funds are very unlikely to exit as $GRAB in the medium-long term. They may trim here and there, sell some Covered Call for degenerated gamblers. "Dumb Money" will be at the mercy of "Smart money" when this trades at $10-$15-$20-$25-$30...

It is what it is. The game hasn't changed!
